speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and when did it first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The facial rash sparing the perioral area is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). Do you have any joint pain or swelling, particularly in your hands or knees?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing joint pain and swelling. Have you noticed any other symptoms, such as nausea or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "slapped cheek" facial rash followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, along with mild prodromal symptoms, is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
